reply_text:
I misread you: I turned XXXX into a requirement that the machine work for any content, and I've withdrawn that. What's been missing is the account you describe: why XXXX fails, field by field, and the least that must replace it. I've made that the first deliverable and written a first cut.

This first cut comes from what clicks 13–20 showed, not from a full read of the code. It follows each text field on the path from task file to terminal receipt:

| Field | Read by | With "XXXX" | Least that must replace it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task status line | field enumeration | Works: unreadable counts as open. Every task stays in the field for ever. | A closed / cancelled / superseded marker from a fixed set. |
| Acceptance criteria | want derivation | Fails: no criteria, no wants, target not admitted. | At least one criterion with a stable id, and a way to check it that isn't the agent ticking its own box. |
| Relation to current focus | classification, feeding the risk term | Fails: class unknown, no score (clicks 15, 17). | One of three values, or a stated default. |
| Interpretation | cascade construction | Fails: the answer is validated against the library and rejected. | An existing pattern id and the want it produces; possibly just an action kind and a want id. |
| Pattern text | the author prompt | The tick runs, but the author has no method. | What to do and what counts as done, in terms of the criterion. |
| Author prompt | the author seat | The seat can't act. | Repo and path, the criterion, permitted scope, reply grammar. |
| Author reply | outcome classification | Fails typed; nothing changes. | An outcome from a fixed set; for a change, repo and sha; for a refusal, a reason kind and the input it names. |
| Reviewer reply | close | Fails typed. | A verdict from a fixed set and the sha reviewed. |
| Refusal reason | nothing reads it today | No effect, which is the click 19/20 defect. | A reason kind and the named missing input, recorded against the attempt. |

So XXXX survives in one field of nine. Five need only a value from a small fixed set or an id. Three need real content: a checkable criterion, a method, and a prompt. Those three are where "well specified tasks and agent behaviour" is required, and none of them has a written minimum today. I think that is the underdeveloped interface you described.

The deliverable produces two short specifications: a minimal task specification and a minimal agent contract. They become the stated hypotheses of the Lean tick model, so the theorems read "given a task and an agent meeting these minimums, the bad behaviour cannot occur". They also supply the fixtures for the pre-click verification.

The order in the draft is now: this specification, then the requirement-to-action table, then the Lean model, then the action rows derived from it, then the readiness records (commit `b6816335c`).

I sent codex-6 the correction and asked them to check and complete the table against the code with file and line for each reader. That is job `invoke-1790751695967-28764-04e7d370`, parked under `park-f11fda49…` with a 60-minute deadline. Once all their parts are in, I'll rewrite the draft once into a clean candidate for agreement and bring it to you.
